correctness.rationale: PASS. The original binary successor rule is equivalent to the integer discrepancy H=a*N_0-b*N_1; a 1 forces next 1 iff H>=0. Every completed 1-run closes with -b<=H<=-1, because the next forced 0 occurs just after crossing zero. When a>b, adding even one intervening zero makes the next starting discrepancy positive. In the explicit prefix 0^b 1^(a+1) 0^m 1^q 0, m is the unique residue 1..b with a*m≡b-1 (mod b) and q=(a*m-b+1)/b. Any later attempted match of the first run must have b+1 zero predecessors; at exactly b the preceding closed-run negative residue prevents length a+1, and elsewhere the run length falls outside. That possible imitation leaves a residual differing from the initial -b by an integer δ in [1,b-1] (none at b=1). The modularly selected second gap then forces q+1 ones, not q. The marker occurs as a legal generating prefix and no shift contains it twice, so no language connector joins it to itself. Language closure converts cylinder membership into a finite generating factor. Independent six-pair bounded state enumerations corroborated nonreturn but do not prove unbounded nontransitivity.
